runtime.name: omp
runtime.configuration: Generated poteto-mode, refactoring, and how Skills plus the implementer role copied into a disposable Git fixture; empty Skill allowlist; one isolated task worktree with patch merge and apply=false.
runtime.permissionProfile: root read/write fixture with one bounded isolated writer and auto-approved inspection and test commands

assertions.evidence: The root explicitly loaded the generated poteto-mode router.
Every Skill and role read came from the disposable repository; filesystem searches stayed inside it and no installed cache was read.
The router selected refactoring because structure changed while observable behavior was required to remain fixed.
The root loaded the generated refactoring and how Skills and followed how's simple path.
The root inspected labels.mjs, the only repository caller/test surface, and the exact four asserted outputs before delegation.
The root ran node --test test/labels.test.mjs before delegation and captured exit 0 with two passing tests.
The root named the duplicated trimming, state selection, and label assembly in renderTask and renderProject.
Before editing, the root named one private renderLabel(kind, name, closed) plus two thin public adapters and no new export.
The session contains exactly one LabelsRefactor child with no retry or replacement.
The child was restricted to labels.mjs and its patch changed only that file.
OMP ran the writer in an isolated worktree and returned an unapplied patch for root integration.
The root checked and applied the patch, inspected the actual diff and status, and reread the final module.
The final module contains one private trim/state/assembly implementation and two thin adapters; only renderTask and renderProject are exported.
After integration the root reran the identical command and captured exit 0 with the same two tests and four exact outputs passing.
The final report compares two duplicated branches with one shared private implementation and names the reduced reconciliation burden.
Only labels.mjs changed; the test hash remained at the fixture baseline.
No commit, push, publication, or pull-request operation occurred.

limitations: Equivalence evidence is bounded to the four observable assertions in the pinned test surface; the repository contains no other callers.
OMP delivery remains D0 overall because the separate plugin-manager D1 gate is unresolved.
